scopeContent.title: De Sitter backgrounds: existence, stability and control
scopeContent.question: Under which source-specific ingredients and approximations can compactifications or related constructions support de Sitter geometry, and what establishes their stability, consistency and effective control?
scopeContent.summary: The original parent has numerical membership but no written scientific scope to endorse. Its contrasts support separate questions about existence, asymptotic control, source matching, evolving quantum backgrounds, effective potentials and statistical stability. Overlapping child-batch titles should not become redundant public branches. Existing scoped questions provide shared destinations across those batches, with distinct applications and alternate homes retained.

systems: Type II compactifications and their related M-theory descriptions
Other string constructions represented in the attributed child reviews
Sourced higher-dimensional gravity and effective supergravity models, with embedding qualifications retained
targets: De Sitter geometry, positive stationary potentials and candidate minima
Moduli stabilization and perturbative or dynamical stability
Source consistency, correction control and finite versus parametric limits
Effective potentials, quantum expansions and state interpretations
Source-defined vacuum statistics and conditional cosmological applications
regimes: Classical, perturbatively corrected and nonperturbative settings kept distinct
Finite parameter values and asymptotic families
Source-specific external dimensions and retained field sectors
AdS and Minkowski comparisons where explicitly supplied
assumptions: Each construction and obstruction retains its own source content, ansatz and approximation
Necessary conditions do not establish solutions, stability or control
Numerical ancestry does not determine scientific parentage
Descendant coverage is attributed to child ledgers rather than independently established by this parent pass
conventions: Positive curvature, a stationary potential, a positive-definite retained Hessian and a controlled metastable vacuum are different claims
Frames, scalar normalization, source signs and coupling definitions remain source-specific
Graph relations describe exact source objects and do not automatically impose premises on a question
Source-scoped singleton access establishes neither atomicity nor cross-source uniqueness
includes: Ordinary and pre-Swampland construction and stability research
Conditional, unsuccessful and disputed proposals with their status preserved
Shared target routes across numerical child batches
Methods, comparisons and applications with explicit relationship types
excludes: A universal existence, impossibility or instability conclusion
A present-day census inferred from dated source statements
Automatic admission of unresolved child replacements
Absorbing black-hole reconstruction, strong CP, defect survival or spectrum classification into the de Sitter-existence target

readingCoverage.readingLimit: Only the supplied contrast descriptions, bounded primary text, exact graph context and attributed child records were assessed. Descendant descriptions were not independently reread. No images, complete papers, numerical replication or later-status checks were available. Preserve child reading limits and source dates, including 1112.3338v4 stamped 17 Apr 2012 with a title-page date of 18 Apr 2012, and 2006.06694v2 dated 18 Sep 2020. The current region is a new proposal requiring later independent review or explicit coordinator adjudication.
readingCoverage.descendantReadingBasis: Attributed immutable child reviews; no claim that this parent pass reread every descendant.

sourceDefinition.title: Vacuum multiplicity, distributions and predictivity
sourceDefinition.question: How do specified compactification models populate vacuum space, and what can their distributions or multiplicities establish?
sourceDefinition.summary: Distinguish multiple vacua at fixed flux, flux ensembles, accumulation near zero vacuum energy, probabilistic explanations and selection-based predictivity.

regimes: Source-defined scans, ensembles and analytic model classes
assumptions: Sampling and ensemble choices do not define a universal landscape measure
conventions: Fixed-flux multiplicity differs from varying-flux statistics
excludes: Promoting observed exclusions to universal theorems
Assuming a higher-dimensional positive cosmological constant has been derived from string theory

sourceDefinition.readingLimit: The excerpts support the fixed-flux multiplicity target; the distribution, typicality and predictivity topics are supplied as descriptions.

targetDefinition.title: Statistical rarity and uplift-induced mixing
targetDefinition.question: Under the stated random-Hessian approximations, how rare are tachyon-free Type IIA de Sitter extrema, and how does increasing vacuum energy affect stability through moduli mixing?
targetDefinition.summary: The source estimates search probabilities and discusses destabilizing off-diagonal terms. These are ensemble-dependent estimates and model observations, not a measured distribution over all string vacua.

targets: Destabilization during increases in vacuum energy
assumptions: A random matrix approximates otherwise complicated Hessian contributions
Mass hierarchies and relative off-diagonal sizes affect the estimate
Treating omitted modes as already stabilized has a limited energy range
conventions: Positive-definite Hessians are a stricter criterion than allowing flat directions
includes: Statistical and uplift-mixing parts of the source question

targetDefinition.readingLimit: Abstract and selected discussion pages only. The supplied v4 is stamped 17 Apr 2012; its title page is dated 18 Apr 2012.

originalProposal.reason: Reuse the same statistical-rarity question through the ensemble route; do not create a second route-dependent copy.
